chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Reaction to hearing the clip
summary: He says no other dancer has voice, dancing and showmanship together, laments Sammy Davis's ruin of the show, and says he is sorry he can no longer do it.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Is it? Well, you got it. Now what other dancer do you know that can come in behind that man, what other dancer? Think about the dancers you know, who's got the voice and who's got the dancing ability and got the showmanship to tie in with such things as you just heard then? All that put together in one. / They ruined that show with Sammy Davis. They ruined that.
You thought George Gershwin wasn't smart in picking me out? You're kidding.
You putting that on again? We're going to get back to where we left off there.
You can keep going. I like to get your feelings about it immediately after it's played.
That's what I just told you about that.
How does it feel listening to it now?
Well, I feel like I'm sorry I can't do it no more. Not right now. No telling when I might be able to do it again.
Because it's still in me, you know. I got something I wanted you to see and now I can't think what I did with it.
